essayStructure.title: Essay Structure That Scores
points: Introduction: define the theme + give a clear thesis in 40–60 words.
Body: 2–3 paragraphs — causes/dimensions, analysis with facts, counterpoint.
Conclusion: balanced way forward; avoid sudden new arguments.

examinerLens.title: How Examiners Read Descriptive Answers
points: Clarity of thought and organisation matter as much as content.
Relevant, recent, factual examples strengthen arguments.
Balance and maturity of tone — especially for socio-political topics.
Language: simple, precise English; avoid slang and extreme adjectives.

commonMistakes.title: Common Mistakes to Avoid
points: Starting without a plan — leads to repetition and weak conclusions.
One-sided political rants instead of multi-dimensional analysis.
Inventing statistics; better to use well-known schemes/institutions.
Ignoring the question's directive words (discuss, examine, critically).
Poor handwriting practice for pen-paper exam (practice on paper too).

dosDonts.title: Do's & Don'ts — IB Descriptive Tone
dos: Stay factual, calm, and constitutionally grounded.
donts: Do not sensationalise security or communal issues.
Do not attack communities or parties; critique policies/institutions.
Do not pad with irrelevant quotations.
